summary.prose: The build adds a src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/ folder in eleven ordered tasks: first the pure parts (input bounds and identifier checks, answer readers over recorded acli output), then the argv, executor and failure mapper, the answer shapes, and the family definer; then the five op tables (work item reads, work item changes, comments and links, projects and auth); then the coverage table, registration and cross-family tests; and last the gated live tests, the disposable-project probe and the documentation. No file under the gh folder is edited, and the one shared-file change is the single registration call in builtins/index.ts.

tasks.title: Jira input layer: limits, identifier patterns, schema bounds, key normaliser, value checks
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/limits.ts (JIRA_LIMITS, JIRA_PATTERNS) and input.ts (jiraInputSchema, normalizeKeys, checkJiraValues). Pure functions over the exported gh op-table types; no gh file is edited.
acceptanceChecks: jiraInputSchema sets maximum 500, 200 and 200 on the search, project list and comment list limit fields, maxItems 50 on every key array and a pattern on every identifier field
51 keys supplied, even with repeats, are refused by the schema; normalizeKeys keeps first-seen order and drops repeats
checkJiraValues refuses a value that starts with '-' in every identifier field (key, keys, project, toProject, projectKey, fromProject, id, user, type name, status, assignee)
no file under src/daemon/tools/builtins/gh is changed

tests.name: jira-inputs.test.ts: jiraInputSchema sets maximum 500, 200 and 200, maxItems 50 and identifier patterns
jira-inputs.test.ts: 51 keys with repeats are refused and normalizeKeys keeps first-seen order
jira-inputs.test.ts: checkJiraValues refuses a leading-dash value in every identifier field

tasks.title: Answer readers over recorded acli output
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/readers.ts with readBatch, readCount, readVisibility (ANSI stripped, count must match rows, heading-only rejected) and parseAuthStatus, and store output recorded from the real acli (docs/plans/tool-registry.md inventory and the approved write probe) as fixture files under src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/__tests__/fixtures.
acceptanceChecks: readBatch is ok only when results is non-empty, every status is SUCCESS and the counts agree; a FAILURE at exit 0 and a partial batch are reported as not ok with the failed and succeeded ids
a clone's new key is read from the success message, not the result id
readCount returns the integer of 'Number of work items in the search: N' and undefined when the line is missing

readVisibility accepts a group table only when '(N total)' equals the parsed rows ('(0 total)' is the only empty), rejects a heading-only or unrecognised body, and accepts a role body only with at least one '- Name' line
parseAuthStatus reads signedIn, site, email and authType and treats an 'unauthorized' text as signed out

tests.name: jira-parsers.test.ts: readBatch handles all SUCCESS, all FAILURE at exit 0, partial, a count mismatch and the clone key from the message
jira-parsers.test.ts: readCount and parseAuthStatus read recorded acli text
jira-parsers.test.ts: readVisibility group and role cases including count mismatch, heading only, unrecognised line and ANSI escapes

tasks.title: Argv, executor and failure mapper
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/exec.ts with jiraArgv (head acli, free text as one --flag=value token, no --paginate), acliExec (runShellBytes, standard input closed, one 'acli jira auth status' probe after an unexplained failure) and jiraFailureOf (precedence and positive-evidence sign-in rule), plus the fake acli test harness _fakeacli.ts.
acceptanceChecks: jiraArgv starts with acli jira, replaces the gh head of buildArgv, passes --yes where acli has it, never --paginate and never --from-json or --generate-json
a free-text value that starts with '-' is passed as one --flag=value token

jiraFailureOf returns missing-tool for a spawn failure or exit 127, timed-out with 'outcome is unknown' for a changing op, and missing-signin only when the probe completed and said unauthorized; a probe that failed on network, time-out or spawn never gives missing-signin
a known rejection text is rejected without running the probe and an output cut at the capture cap is a failure

tests.name: jira-argv.test.ts: jiraArgv head, --yes, literal --json, finite --limit, never --paginate and free text as one --flag=value token
jira-failures.test.ts: jiraFailureOf precedence and the probe rules
jira-failures.test.ts: not installed, not signed in, network probe, time-out and truncated output through a fake acli

tasks.title: Answer shapes and shared answer builders
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/schemas.ts (the answer shapes: view, search, count, attachment, watcher, comment list, visibility, link, project, auth status, and the changing-op shape {ok, target, message}) and answers.ts with the shared builders for a batch result, a success-mark text result, a JSON read and a count, built on the readers of t2. Only key, id, name and the properties callers need are typed; the rest passes through as unknown.
acceptanceChecks: the batch builder turns a not-ok batch into a rejected failure that lists each failed id and, when some succeeded, each succeeded id with the words 'the batch was partly applied'
the success-mark builder accepts text that starts with the success mark and turns any other exit-0 text into a rejected failure with acli's text in original
the JSON builders type only key, id and name (watchers accountId) so an extra or null property never fails a call
each shape accepts the recorded answer of its op and rejects a wrong literal op

tests.name: jira-answers.test.ts: the batch builder lists failed and succeeded ids and says the batch was partly applied
jira-answers.test.ts: the success-mark builder rejects any other exit-0 text
jira-output-schemas.test.ts: each shape accepts its recorded answer, passes extra properties through and rejects a wrong literal op

tasks.title: defineJiraFamily, approval and preview
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/family.ts: defineJiraFamily takes the ops, builds the input schema with jiraInputSchema, runs refuseInput with dashSafe true, checkJiraValues, normalizeKeys, jiraArgv and acliExec, maps failures with jiraFailureOf, calls the op's answer builder, wraps the tool in withGhFailureNet and returns a GhFamilyTool; approval is a function of the op (an unknown op is destructive) with a small preview. Tested on a small table of sample ops.
acceptanceChecks: a family built from sample ops refuses unknown ops, missing, extra and exclusive-group fields through the run-time input check before acli runs
a reader failure comes back from executeTool as kind rejected and a builder that returns data outside its op's union, or no data, comes back as kind schema-mismatch
the approval function returns none, common or destructive per op and destructive for an unknown op
the returned value is a GhFamilyTool carrying its ops and no gh file is changed

tests.name: jira-family.test.ts: a sample family refuses unknown ops, missing, extra and exclusive-group fields before acli runs
jira-output-validation.test.ts: a builder that returns data outside its union, or no data, is schema-mismatch through executeTool
jira-failures.test.ts: reader failures are rejected through executeTool
jira-approval.test.ts: the approval function per op and an unknown op is destructive and denied with no client

tasks.title: jira_workitem reads (5 ops)
tasks.summary: Create src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/workitem.ts with the jira_workitem family and its read ops: view, search, count, attachment-list and watcher-list, with their fields, rules, class none, limits (30 s, search and count 60 s) and answer builders.
acceptanceChecks: view, search, count, attachment-list and watcher-list are class none and return their declared shapes from recorded output
search and count take exactly one of jql and filter, search passes a finite --limit within 1 to 500 (default 50) and never --paginate, and count reads the 'Number of work items in the search' line
the argv of each op matches the acli command and flags

tests.name: jira-workitem-reads.test.ts: each read op returns its declared shape and its argv matches acli
jira-workitem-reads.test.ts: search and count take exactly one of jql and filter and search is limited

tasks.title: jira_workitem changes (10 ops)
tasks.summary: Extend src/daemon/tools/builtins/jira/workitem.ts with create, edit, transition, assign, clone, archive, unarchive, delete, attachment-delete and watcher-remove, with their fields, rules, classes, 60 s limits and answer builders.
acceptanceChecks: create, edit, transition, assign, clone, archive, unarchive and watcher-remove are common; delete and attachment-delete are destructive
edit, transition, assign, clone, archive, unarchive and delete take keys only (one to 50), refuse jql, filter and from-file, and pass --yes
transition takes the target status by name; clone reads the new key from the message; a FAILURE result at exit 0 comes back as a rejected failure
the argv of each op matches the acli command and flags and each op's recorded answer fits its output member

tests.name: jira-workitem-changes.test.ts: each changing op returns {ok, target, message} and its argv matches acli
jira-workitem-changes.test.ts: keys only, repeated keys sent once, jql, filter and from-file refused
jira-workitem-changes.test.ts: a FAILURE result at exit 0 and a partial batch are rejected failures

tasks.title: jira_comment (5 ops) and jira_link (4 ops)
tasks.summary: Create comment.ts (list, create, update, delete, visibility) and link.ts (list, types, create, delete) with fields, rules, classes, limits and answer builders.
acceptanceChecks: comment list/visibility and link list/types are none, comment create/update and link create are common, comment delete and link delete are destructive
comment list passes a finite --limit within 1 to 200; visibility takes exactly one of group and role and role needs project; a comment body comes only from the body field
link create and delete and comment update and delete succeed only on the success mark; each op's recorded answer fits its output member

tests.name: jira-comment-link.test.ts: every comment and link op returns its declared shape and its argv matches acli
jira-comment-link.test.ts: text commands without the success mark are rejected and visibility rules are enforced

tasks.title: jira_project (7 ops) and jira_auth (1 op)
tasks.summary: Create project.ts (list, view, create from an existing project, update, archive, restore, delete) and auth.ts (status) with fields, rules, classes, limits and answer builders; the project mutation readers accept the success mark only until the probe records the real text.
acceptanceChecks: project create requires fromProject, key and name and builds acli jira project create --from-project SRC --key NEW --name N with optional --description, --url and --lead-email, never --from-json or --generate-json
project archive and delete are destructive, create, update and restore are common, list and view are none; list takes exactly one of limit (1 to 200, default 30) and recent
jira_auth status is class none and reads the sign-in state without any model call

tests.name: jira-project-auth.test.ts: every project op and auth status returns its declared shape and its argv matches acli
jira-project-auth.test.ts: project create needs fromProject and a non-company-managed source is a rejected failure

tasks.title: Coverage table, registration and cross-family tests
tasks.summary: Create coverage.ts (JIRA_COVERAGE, JIRA_UNSUPPORTED, EXCLUDED_BY_AMENDMENT from the ac1 amendment) and index.ts with registerJiraTools; add the one call to registerBuiltinTools in src/daemon/tools/builtins/index.ts after registerGhTools; add the coverage, parser canary, family, output-schema, approval, spawn-only and registration tests.
acceptanceChecks: registerJiraTools adds exactly five tool ids (jira_workitem, jira_comment, jira_link, jira_project, jira_auth) with 32 ops, 12 none, 14 common and 6 destructive, and changes no existing tool id

every command of the installed acli jira is covered or in the amended exclusion list, checked against an independently written REQUIRED_OPS inventory, and a transition by id and a list of transitions are named unsupported and are not ops
with fake jira, jira-cli and go-jira on PATH only acli is run across every op

tests.name: jira-coverage.test.ts: every acli command is covered or in the amended exclusion list, checked against REQUIRED_OPS, and the exclusion list equals the amendment table
jira-coverage.test.ts: JIRA_UNSUPPORTED names a transition by id and the list of transitions and neither is a registered op
jira-coverage.test.ts: classes are 6 destructive, 12 none, 14 common, 32 in all
jira-parser.test.ts: the commands and flags of the real acli match the coverage table, including the project flags (skipped when acli is absent)
jira-spawn-only.test.ts: with fake jira, jira-cli and go-jira on PATH only acli is run across every op
jira-family.test.ts: the five tools and 32 ops are registered and each op returns its declared shape
jira-registration.test.ts: registerJiraTools adds exactly five tool ids and changes no existing one

tasks.title: Live tests, project probe and documentation
tasks.summary: Add the INSRC_LIVE_TESTS-gated live tests (reads, a work item create and delete, and the disposable-project probe gated by a company-managed source project key, a scratch project key and a lead email), run the read-only and work item ones, run the project probe only after the user confirms the three values, record the real success text of each project mutation as fixtures, and document the five tools, their classes and the recorded text in docs/plans/tool-registry.md.
acceptanceChecks: the live tests skip with a reason when INSRC_LIVE_TESTS or the probe variables are not set
the read-only live ops return their declared shape against the signed-in site

the project probe runs only after the user confirms the three values; it then creates the scratch project from the source, updates, archives, restores and deletes it, deletes it even if a step fails, and stores the success text of each as fixtures that the project readers are tested against; if the site refuses project creation the refusal text is recorded and the project readers stay on the success mark
docs/plans/tool-registry.md lists the five tools, their classes and the recorded project mutation text

tests.name: jira-live.test.ts: read ops view, search, count, list, types, status and visibility return their declared shape
jira-live.test.ts: one work item create then delete in a scratch project with cleanup of any clone
jira-live.test.ts: the disposable-project probe records the real success text of each project mutation
jira-docs.test.ts: docs/plans/tool-registry.md lists the five tools, their classes and the excluded and unsupported lists

testStrategyCoverage.lldStrategyItem: readBatch: all SUCCESS, all FAILURE at exit 0, partial, count mismatch, clone key from the message
readCount, parseAuthStatus on recorded acli text
readVisibility: group with a matching '(N total)', group with '(0 total)', count that differs from the rows, heading only, unrecognised line, role with and without '- Name' lines, ANSI escapes
jiraInputSchema: maximum 500, 200 and 200 on the limit fields, maxItems 50 on key arrays, patterns on identifiers; 51 keys with repeats refused; normalizeKeys keeps first-seen order

checkJiraValues and the schema patterns: a leading-dash value in every flag-valued identifier (key, keys, project, toProject, projectKey, fromProject, id, user, type name, status, assignee) and in a positional is refused, and refuseInput runs with dashSafe true

jiraArgv: head acli, --yes where acli has it, literal --json, finite --limit only on search, project list and comment list, never --paginate, free text joined as one '--flag=value' token including a value that starts with '-'

jiraArgv for project create is exactly 'acli jira project create --from-project SRC --key NEW --name N' plus optional --description, --url and --lead-email, and never --from-json or --generate-json; project update uses --project-key; archive, restore and delete use --key and no --yes
jiraFailureOf precedence and the probe rules (missing-signin only on positive evidence)
approval function per op and an unknown op
jira_workitem, jira_comment, jira_link, jira_project and jira_auth: every op returns the declared shape
reader failures are rejected: a FAILURE result at exit 0, a text command without the success mark, an unreadable count or visibility body each come back from executeTool as kind rejected

executor output validation is schema-mismatch: with an answer builder that returns data outside its op's output union (and one that returns no data), executeTool returns kind schema-mismatch and the family does not relabel it as rejected
not installed (exit 127), not signed in (unauthorized probe), network failure probe, time-out, truncated output on a read that takes no limit
project create from a non-company-managed source: acli's refusal text reaches the caller as a rejected failure
a spawn-only check: with fake jira, jira-cli and go-jira on PATH only acli is ever run

input rules at run time: exclusive groups, 50 key cap, repeated keys sent once, changing ops refuse jql, filter and from-file, a missing required field (project create without fromProject) and an unknown op are refused by the run-time input check
each defineJiraFamily result is a GhFamilyTool carrying its ops (the same shape the gh families return); no concrete compile-time input or output type is asserted

jira-coverage: every command of the installed acli jira is covered or in the approved exclusion list, checked against an independently written REQUIRED_OPS inventory; the exclusion list equals the table of the section 's6 scope amendment to ac1' in docs/plans/tool-registry.md
JIRA_UNSUPPORTED names a transition by id and the list of transitions, and neither is a registered op
output schemas accept the recorded answer of each op and reject a wrong literal op
classes: the 6 destructive ops are destructive, 12 are none, 14 are common, 32 in all
jira-parser against the real acli --help (canary, skipped when acli is absent), including the flags of project create, update, archive, restore and delete
read ops: view, search, count, list, types, status, visibility
one create then delete of a work item in a scratch project with cleanup of any clone

a disposable-project probe, additionally gated by three environment variables (a company-managed source project key, a scratch project key for the new project, and a lead email): create it from the source, update, archive, restore and delete it, recording the real success text of each as a fixture file before the project mutation readers are accepted; the probe deletes the project even when a step fails, and skips with a reason when the variables are not set
registerJiraTools adds exactly five tool ids and changes no existing one
docs/plans/tool-registry.md lists the five tools, their classes and the excluded and unsupported lists
